caption: The video captures an extreme macro close-up of a person's open eye against a black background, the pale iris catching a bright ring-light reflection on the cornea. Long eyelashes are beaded with many tiny clinging water droplets, and a larger droplet rests on the upper lid near the brow. On the left of the frame, a droplet is already mid-descent as the clip opens, moving downward through the darkness. A second droplet enters near the top edge while the first is still falling, and the first soon exits off the bottom edge. The second continues its downward pass and leaves the frame, after which a brief interval shows no droplet in transit. A third droplet then enters near the top and repeats the vertical fall beside the eye before disappearing. Throughout, the iris, pupil and corneal highlight remain largely in place, so the visible movement is chiefly the slow descent of these droplets, while the open eye and bead-studded lashes persist.
